source: flac16/48kHz; Matrix Source 1 (shnid 137334): Recording Info: SBD > Dat Master (Panasonic SV-3700/48k); Transfer Info: Dat Master (Sony R500) > Sound Devices 744T > Samplitude Pro X3 Suite > FLAC/48k and Source 2 (shnid 106551): Recording info: (Handheld/ORTF/110^/FOB/DFC/Row20) B&K 4011s > Neumann BS48i-2 > Panasonic SV-255 > DAT(m); Transfer info: DAT(m) > Sony DTC-59ES > SPDIF > Tascam HD-P2 > Audacity (16/48 > 16/44) > CDWave > FLAC; DAT(m) sourced by Alan Schmit

ai_review.summary: Matrix from the odd‑year ’93 with decent sound despite the usual kick‑drum pop, offering a listenable show though no standout moments are highlighted.
ai_review.review: The matrix capture is praised for sounding good to the reviewer’s ears and receiving a thank‑you note for its overall quality, even though 1993 board quirks (kick‑drum popping and occasional phase issues) are noted. Musical commentary is sparse – Jerry’s playing is described as “lucid” with a Wolf‑style tone, while Bob Weir’s lyric delivery on “Wang Dang” draws criticism. Overall the recording is listenable but the performance details remain unremarkable.

ai_rating.rationale: Two reviews give divergent scores (3★ and 5★). Recording quality is judged good for a matrix despite known ’93 kick‑drum issues, but the show itself receives little praise or criticism, leading to an overall moderate rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Typical 1993 board quirks – noticeable pop from Billy's kick drum mic and potential phase issues in matrices, but this particular matrix sounds clean to the reviewer and received a thank‑you for its nice sound.

show_quality.setlist_flow: No specific comments on set structure; reviewers focused on recording characteristics rather than musical flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as lucid with a Wolf‑style guitar tone.
band_member_comments.Bob: Criticized for mangling the "Wang Dang" lyrics.
